cold_email.subject: Interest in Apprenticeship Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear National Film & Television School Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Apprenticeship Coordinator opportunity with National Film & Television School at National Film & Television School.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Implicit Signals
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Our team builds classification and evaluation systems that give post-training and research teams fast, reliable feedback on model behavior. We combine machine learning and production engineering to make these capabilities accurate, efficient, and useful at scale, helping researchers assess changes and improve models and products. We work closely with research teams to develop useful measurements and make them practical to run. Our work spans classifier development, rigorous evaluation, and efficient production inference, with ownership from initial experimentation through deployment and continued improvement. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a machine learning engineer to develop new classification and evaluation capabilities and bring them into production. You’ll help turn open-ended questions about model behavior into well-defined ML problems, build methods that address them, and establish how reliably those methods work. This role combines traditional machine learning, model evaluation, and real-time engineering. You’ll own classifiers throughout their lifecycle, including supervised fine-tuning, distillation, evaluation, deployment, and production inference. You’ll work closely with researchers to identify valuable problems and with software engineers to make promising approaches useful at scale. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Build, deploy, and operate production classification and evaluation systems that provide useful feedback to post-training and research teams. - Optimize production inference, including model serving, batching, caching, throughput, latency, compute utilization, and cost. - Train and optimize classifiers using supervised fine-tuning and distillation, validating quality and efficiency before deployment. - Own the reliability and observability of deployed classifiers, diagnose production issues, and improve their performance over time. - Design rigorous evaluations that assess accuracy, calibration, generalization, and potential measurement bias while guiding production tradeoffs. - Partner with software engineers to integrate models into reliable execution systems and support safe rollouts. - Build reusable engineering tools that make classifier training, evaluation, deployment, and iteration faster and more repeatable. - Work with post-training researchers and data scientists to translate their needs into modeling objectives, evaluation criteria, and production requirements. YOUR BACKGROUND MIGHT LOOK SOMETHING LIKE - Experience taking ML projects from problem formulation and experimentation through production deployment. - Strong foundations in supervised learning, statistics, and experimental design. - Practical experience evaluating models, investigating systematic errors, and working with imperfect labels. - Strong software engineering skills and the ability to build maintainable production ML systems. - Experience reasoning about inference performance and the tradeoffs between quality, latency, and compute cost. - The ability to combine careful scientific judgment with a practical approach to shipping and operating software. - Comfort working closely with researchers and engineers on open-ended problems. - Fluency in using AI agents to move quickly across multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment. - Experience with model distillation, representation learning, calibration, or efficient inference is a plus. cold_email.subject: Interest in Manufacturing Associate I, INT — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Moderna Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Manufacturing Associate I, INT opportunity with Moderna at Moderna.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Clinical Oncology Spec — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Clinical Oncology Spec opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Corporate Systems team runs the core collaboration platforms everyone here works in and builds the tooling and automation behind IT. That responsibility extends to the companies we acquire. Their people, devices, and systems have to come into Anthropic securely. You'll own the IT side of Anthropic's acquisitions: due diligence, integration planning, and integration. Before close, you'll assess a company's IT environment and give the deal team a clear read on risk and effort. You'll define the technical integration plan and its requirements: what moves, where it lands, in what order, what has to be ready on day one, and how each security gap gets closed. After close, you'll carry out that plan and bring the company's people, devices, and systems onto our stack. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll hold admin, write code, build automation, run the cutovers yourself and bring in other teams when the work calls for their expertise or support. You'll lead this work for IT Engineering and partner with Security, Corporate Development, Legal, People, and Finance at every stage. M&A will be your primary focus and responsibility, but you'll be a full member of the Corporate Systems team; taking part in planning and reviews, using and contributing to the team’s tooling, and contributing to the roadmap. Early on, M&A will be most of your work, including using Claude to automate the repeatable parts of diligence and integration. As that automation matures, and when M&A load is light, you'll contribute to other parts of the team’s roadmap. Responsibilities Lead technical IT due diligence: assess a company's identity, applications, endpoints, and infrastructure, and brief the deal team on risk and effort before close Find the gaps between an acquired environment and Anthropic's security model, rate them, and build the mitigations into the integration plan Define the technical integration plan and its requirements: what moves, where it lands, in what order, and what has to be ready on day one Run the integration: take over administration, migrate people, devices, and data, and retire what's no longer needed, with support from other IT Engineering teams as required. Work with Business Technology, Client Platform, Corporate Network, IT Operations, and Security on their parts of each integration Keep Corporate Development, Legal, People, Finance, and the acquired company's team clear on where IT stands Build a repeatable IT M&A playbook and automate as much of it as possible with Claude When M&A work is light, contribute to core Corporate Systems projects You may be a good fit if you have 8+ years as a hands-on engineer in corporate IT. You have designed and shipped systems, carried out migrations or integrations yourself, and owned at least one area end-to-end, with experience supporting other areas: identity, applications, endpoints, or corporate infrastructure Experience administering enterprise identity and collaboration platforms such as Google Workspace, Slack, and an SSO provider, and working code in Python or similar against their SaaS APIs Working knowledge of endpoint management and security concepts, enough to lead diligence on an unfamiliar fleet A proven ability to understand an unfamiliar IT environment quickly and deliver a prioritized view of risk to non-specialists A record of leading technical projects that span several teams and run to a fixed date, while doing much of the engineering yourself Comfort working autonomously, with ambiguity and confidential information Clear communication with executives, legal and corporate development teams, and engineers at acquired companies Strong candidates may also have Prior M&A, carve-out, or company-to-company migration experience Experience across the full stack: endpoints, systems, applications, and infrastructure Hands-on experience managing a device fleet or running an MDM Experience working in or alongside a security team A record of building tooling that replaces manual IT work Using Claude or similar tools as a core part of how you work Representative projects Assess an acquired company's IT environment that nobody here has seen and produce a prioritized integration plan within days Design a way to size integration effort and risk for a company of any shape or size Automate bringing acquired people and devices onto Anthropic's identity and device management Write the IT risk memo for a live deal and present it to Corporate Development and Security leadership Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $325,000 — $360,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, ML Infrastructure
jobs.description: About Arc Institute Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco. Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone. Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action: Virtual Cell Initiative : Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets, accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials. Alzheimer's Disease Initiative : Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes. More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding. About the position You'll join Arc's Infrastructure Engineering team and own the data and evaluation of ML infrastructure for Arc's virtual cell models. You'll start with two systems: our Model Performance Dashboard, which benchmarks those models, and the pipeline that turns single-cell data into their training sets. You'll set the technical direction for both and connect them, so every new dataset version is judged by what it does to the models. Later in your first year, the role widens into the engineering that makes the ML team's training and evaluation run fast and at scale, lab-in-the-loop infrastructure, validation frameworks for agent-written software, and Arc's rules for what research data we bring in, keep and share. The role consolidates ownership that is split across several teams today. Why this position could be the best job you’ve ever had You will contribute to building a virtual cell. Your evals show which data makes Arc's models better, and the answer shapes which experiments Arc's labs run next. You will own the platform end to end, and you work directly with the ML researchers and scientists who rely on it. About you You finish what you own, and you fix what's broken without being asked. You're curious about the biology, enough to learn single-cell perturbation data and argue about what an eval should measure. You're steady when priorities shift. Research is high-risk, so you test ideas early and change course when the evidence says to. You don't wait on scarce expert time. If proving a dataset's value means running the model evals yourself, you run them. In this position you will Own how Arc measures the performance of its virtual cell models, starting with the backend of our Model Performance Dashboard, which you'll take over within your first two months. Decide with the ML team which evaluation tools they need, then design and build them so researchers can evaluate and compare models themselves, and measure what each dataset version does to model performance. Redesign the pipeline that turns single-cell data into training sets for our virtual cell models, then run it with AI agents: agents find, process and curate datasets, and automated quality checks, not manual review, decide whether a dataset version is ready for model training. Own the lab-in-the-loop infrastructure that turns model performance results into the case for what Arc's labs should test next, working directly with the science leads who design those experiments . Build or buy validation frameworks (tests, evals, QC gates, policies) that let agent-written code and apps ship without line-by-line human review. Start with our team, where you'll also own how we work with coding agents, then extend them to apps that scientists across Arc build themselves. Own the engineering that makes the ML team's training and evaluation run fast, reliably and at scale. The ML team owns the research and the models. Once a model is ready to push, it enters the train-and-eval CI system you own, which feeds our Model Performance Dashboard. You'll also make multi-node training a supported path, track down distributed-training failures, and measure and raise throughput and GPU utilization (MFU) on clusters that Arc IT operates. Requirements Bachelor’s degree with 8 years of relevant experience, or Master’s degree with 6 years of relevant experience. You've owned a production data or ML platform that researchers depend on, end to end (pipelines, storage, versioning), and set its technical direction. You design and build systems with AI tools and agents, and you make their output verifiable with evals, QC gates or tests before anyone relies on it. You've learned an unfamiliar technical domain well enough to make design calls in it. You work directly with stakeholders to find requirements, with no PM in between. You make the people around you better through code review, pairing and writing patterns down. You've diagnosed and fixed performance problems in Python or PyTorch systems with profilers and measurements: GPU utilization, memory, data loading. Work onsite in our Palo Alto office at least 3 days a week. Preferred Qualifications You've worked with single-cell or perturbation data (AnnData/h5ad). You've built or run model evaluations: benchmarks, eval harnesses, PyTorch/GPU inference. You've run multi-node distributed training (DDP/FSDP, NCCL, SLURM) or raised a training job's throughput. This is a plus, not a requirement: we care more that you learn it fast with agents and show the numbers moved. You've led an effort with one or two other engineers. The base salary range for this position is $ 191,000 to $237,000 . These amounts reflect the range of base salary that the Institute reasonably would expect to pay a new hire or internal candidate for this position. The actual base compensation paid to any individual for this position may vary depending on factors such as experience, market conditions, education/training, skill level, and whether the compensation is internally equitable, and does not include bonuses, commissions, differential pay, other forms of compensation, or benefits. This position is also eligible to receive an annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors. In addition to the Base Salary and Annual Bonus above, you will be eligible to participate in the Institute’s Compound Cash Grant Program (the “CCGP”). The CCGP is a program designed to offer multi-year cash grants providing for a fixed dollar amount paid out in semi-annual installments to reward employees for staying and contributing to the Institute. As soon as reasonably practical after your start date, you will receive a grant letter describing the terms of your award under the CCGP.

cold_email.body:
Dear Arc Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Software Engineer, ML Infrastructure opportunity with Arc Institute at Arc Institute.

I am especially interested in the lab's use of single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data to connect molecular mechanisms with therapeutic questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built reproducible genomics workflows and enjoy translating complex biological questions into clear, testable computational analyses.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About Anthropic Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About Beneficial Deployments Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most. About the Role We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team. Our goal is for Claude to close the loop on scientific discovery, and a significant part of this is helping Claude to drive scientific hardware and software. You'll help deploy the Model Hardware Standard (MHS) to labs doing the world’s most important research. You’ll scale what you learn in the field by contributing back to the standard, building scalable assets, and driving associated internal product and research direction. Responsibilities Work with labs to automate their experiments end-to-end with Claude - from advising, to prototyping, to writing production code. Drive product, engineering and research direction based on field experience - e.g. building evals to measure limitations of our models in the physical world (capabilities and safety), developing new features on MHS, etc. Scale your impact to the long tail of labs through reusable cookbooks, documentation, and other assets. Be an EMEA ambassador for Claude in the lab - you’ll both inspire and build trust with scientific audiences, from small settings to large conferences. This role will require significant travel You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have Hands-on experience connecting software to lab robots and instruments (liquid handlers, plate readers, scheduling software, LIMS), ideally in an automated lab. Strong engineering skills: you can take an LLM-powered tool from prototype to production code, and write evals to measure its performance. A scientist's instinct for how experiments work: you can spot what's worth automating, and where AI might fail or be unsafe in the physical world. Experience working directly with external customers or partners in a technical role. Clear written and verbal communication: you’ll write docs other labs can use without you and give talks that inspire and earn researchers' trust. A scrappy mentality–comfortable wearing multiple hats, building from scratch, driving clarity in ambiguous situations, and doing whatever it takes to further the mission. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: £225,000 — £255,000 GBP Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. The challenge is to make reliable decisions from noisy, delayed, and incomplete signals. You will combine machine learning, optimization, and experimentation to improve incremental growth and long-term user value within budget and efficiency constraints. You will own this work from problem formulation and prototyping through deployment, evaluation, and ongoing operation. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to eligible employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Build budget allocation algorithms. Adjust budgets and spending rates as performance changes, balancing responsiveness with stability when feedback is delayed or noisy. Build in spend limits, monitoring, and safe fallback behavior. - Model marketing response and user value. jobs.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase . Coinbase is looking for an experienced SEC Reporting Manager to join our Financial Reporting organization. Reporting to the Director, SEC Reporting, this role will serve as a key owner of Coinbase’s external reporting process, including Forms 10-Q, 10-K, 8-K, earnings release support, and related audit and control activities. This role will coordinate with Controllership, Technical Accounting, FP&A, Investor Relations, Legal, Tax, and external auditors, while also helping drive improvements to our reporting infrastructure, Workiva processes, and disclosure operating model in a fast-moving public-company environment. What you’ll do: Own major portions of the end-to-end 10-Q / 10-K / 8-K production cycle, including calendar management, drafting coordination, review workflows, tie-outs, and final filing support. Lead complex disclosure areas, translating accounting, business, and operational changes into clear and decision-useful external reporting. Partner cross-functionally with Controllership, Technical Accounting, FP&A, Investor Relations, Legal, Tax, and external auditors to resolve judgmental issues and deliver timely, accurate filings. Drive structural improvements to SEC reporting, including Workiva, source-data flows, supporting templates, review controls, and process documentation. Support audit requests, quarterly board / audit committee materials, and other ad hoc analyses tied to external reporting. Coach and elevate junior team members through review, process discipline, and operating best practices. Required Skills and Experience: 9+ years of relevant experience in SEC reporting, external reporting, or public-company financial reporting, including recent hands-on ownership of 10-Q / 10-K processes. CPA or equivalent required. Strong knowledge of US GAAP, SEC disclosure requirements, SOX controls, and public-company reporting mechanics. Demonstrated experience owning complex disclosures, coordinating auditors, and managing cross-functional stakeholders under tight deadlines. Experience with Workiva (Wdesk), NetSuite, and spreadsheet-based analytical review in a controlled reporting environment. Strong written judgment, project management, and communication skills, with the ability to improve ambiguous or evolving processes. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. cold_email.subject: Interest in Medical Analytics Care Gaps & Customer Segmentation Leader — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Medical Analytics Care Gaps & Customer Segmentation Leader opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Compensation Operations Analyst
jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI’s People team supports a complex, rapidly growing organization of researchers, engineers, and business teams. The Compensation function ensures accuracy, scalability, and operational excellence across all compensation tools, systems, and data flows. About the Role We’re hiring a Compensation Operations Analyst to build and run the systems, tools, and processes that power compensation at OpenAI. This role is deeply operational and technical: you will configure HRIS modules, manage compensation tools end-to-end, maintain pristine data quality, and ensure compensation cycles run flawlessly. You’ll partner closely with People Systems, Total Rewards, Finance, and vendors to keep our compensation infrastructure accurate, scalable, and audit-ready. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Own configuration and day-to-day operations of compensation tools and HRIS compensation modules. - Manage annual and off-cycle compensation processes, ensuring data integrity, testing, quality assurance, and on-time execution. - Build and maintain compensation datasets, dashboards, audits, and data flows across systems. - Lead compensation vendor relationships, including implementation, troubleshooting, and data submissions. - Diagnose and resolve system issues, identify root causes, and drive process and tooling improvements. - Partner with People Systems and Engineering to enhance architecture, workflows, and automation. - Ensure high data accuracy across compensation systems and proactively identify gaps, risks, or anomalies. - Translate technical or complex compensation system issues into clear guidance for stakeholders. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 5+ years of experience in compensation operations, HRIS systems, or total rewards tooling in high-growth or technology environments. - Have strong HRIS configuration experience, especially with compensation planning modules; Workday experience is preferred. - Have advanced Excel skills and familiarity with BI tools such as Tableau or Looker; SQL or Python experience is a plus. - Bring rigor and precision to data auditing, validation, and lifecycle management. - Can manage and optimize tools at scale while navigating fast-moving environments. - Communicate effectively across functions and are comfortable working with technical partners. - Are action-oriented, organized, and reliable under tight deadlines. - Have a strong ownership mindset and a bias toward simple, scalable systems. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. cold_email.subject: Interest in Mgr Software Engineering, R&D PPM Tech Lead — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Mgr Software Engineering, R&D PPM Tech Lead opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Fulfillment Planning
jobs.description: About the Team The Fulfillment Planning team builds the intelligence that powers DoorDash’s logistics network. We optimize how deliveries are planned and executed across the full delivery lifecycle, improving customer experience, merchant outcomes, Dasher efficiency, and DoorDash profitability. Our mission is to improve fulfillment quality while reducing fulfillment cost. We do this by applying machine learning, optimization, and systems engineering to the core decisions behind assignment, routing, batching, timing, and fulfillment estimation. The team works on some of DoorDash’s most important logistics systems, including: The core assignment engine that matches deliveries with Dashers in real time. Real-time ETA and fulfillment estimation systems for consumers, Dashers, and merchants across diverse geographies and all business lines. Assignment and planning algorithms for specialized delivery types, including grocery, retail, parcel, and catering. ML models and optimization algorithms that shape demand, improve service quality, and reduce cost. Tier-0 logistics services that require high reliability, low latency, and strong operational discipline. The team also builds reusable ML systems and modeling patterns that scale across DoorDash’s logistics ecosystem. This role will help define the technical direction and best practices for logistics ML at DoorDash. About the Role We’re looking for a Staff Machine Learning Engineer to lead the design, development, and deployment of large-scale production ML systems that drive real-time decisioning across DoorDash’s fulfillment ecosystem. You will start by owning ML systems for assignment and fulfillment estimation, partnering closely with Product, Data Science, Engineering, and Platform teams to improve delivery quality, cost, and efficiency. Over time, you may also contribute to adjacent areas such as batching, fulfillment execution, demand shaping, and logistics optimization across DoorDash’s business lines. This is a high-impact individual contributor role for someone who enjoys building 0→1 ML systems, operating at Staff-level scope, and influencing technical direction across multiple teams. You will define architectures, set modeling and deployment standards, mentor other engineers, and help shape how DoorDash applies machine learning to logistics at scale. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Own and build foundational ML systems that directly impact delivery quality, cost, and overall logistics efficiency across DoorDash. Work on challenging, real-world machine learning problems , including real-time assignment, routing, and fulfillment estimation. Lead 0→1 ML initiatives , defining how machine learning and optimization are applied across fulfillment products. Influence architecture, strategy, and execution for a Tier-0 service critical to DoorDash’s logistics platform. Collaborate closely with Product, Data Science, and Platform Engineering in a highly cross-functional environment. Establish best practices for model development, deployment, monitoring, retraining, and governance. Define and lead DoorDash’s cutting-edge AI vision for logistics: an LLM-inspired foundation model for intelligence across logistics Mentor other engineers and raise the technical bar for logistics ML across the organization. We’re excited about you because… You have 8+ years of industry experience building and deploying production-scale machine learning systems. You have strong machine learning fundamentals and know how to apply them to large-scale production systems. You are fluent in Python You have hands-on experience with modern ML frameworks, especially deep learning frameworks. You have designed, launched, and operated mission-critical ML models or systems in production, including monitoring, retraining, reliability, and governance. You can lead complex technical projects end to end and influence stakeholders across multiple teams or organizations. You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences. You are comfortable operating in ambiguous problem spaces and turning 0→1 ideas into production systems. You have built or shipped large-scale ML models for recommendation, ads, marketplace, logistics, or other domains. You have experience with knowledge distillation from large teacher models into efficient production models. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others. To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here . See below for paid time off details: For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year. For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week). The national base pay range for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado. $203,500 — $299,300 USD About DoorDash At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. jobs.title: Tech Lead Manager, AI Evaluations
jobs.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: The bottleneck in building reliable and useful AI systems isn’t writing code anymore. It’s knowing what good looks like, applying that knowledge and experience from production usage into building rigorous evals, and using those evals to guide continuous product self-improvement loops. As the Tech Lead Manager of AI Evaluations, you will lead a team of applied AI scientists and engineers and build the evaluation strategy and platform that helps Glean ship delightful and reliable AI experiences. You will make evaluation a continuous part of how we develop and operate models, harnesses, assistants, agents, and other AI products at Glean. You’ll guide the team in translating emerging AI/ML research into reliable evaluation systems, build scalable, efficient and reusable eval infrastructure and trusted quality signals, and work across R&D, product, and marketing teams to turn evaluation results into better products and customer outcomes. You will: Own the AI evaluation eng roadmap and technical direction end to end: from defining what success means and building the evaluation platform to integrating results into release and product decisions. Build scalable, reusable evaluation infrastructure for datasets, experiments, graders, trace capture and replay, result analysis, and dashboards. Make evaluations reproducible, versioned, cost-aware, and easy for product and engineering teams to use. Create and maintain representative evaluation sets from expert-curated examples, appropriately governed production signals, synthetic cases, and historical failures. Cover common workflows, edge cases, long-tail requests, adversarial inputs, and important user and domain slices; protect held-out acceptance sets from tuning leakage. Define a balanced quality measurement system for AI products, including correctness, groundedness, retrieval and context relevance, completeness, instruction following, citation quality, user preference, and task success. For agents, evaluate tool selection and arguments, multi-step trajectories, policy compliance, recovery, and final task state, not just the final response. Develop a fit-for-purpose mix of deterministic checks, model-based graders (including LLM-based autograders), and human evaluation. Establish clear rubrics; validate and calibrate automated judges against human judgments; and measure evaluator reliability and limitations so teams can trust and interpret scores. Integrate evaluation into development and operations: fast CI regression checks, broader pre-release suites, model and prompt comparisons, and sampled production evaluation. Build feedback loops from user feedback and production traces into new test cases, and use monitoring, canaries, and experiments to detect regressions and drift. Make quality tradeoffs measurable by connecting evaluation outcomes to latency, reliability, and cost. Help teams diagnose failures by slice and trace, prioritize improvements, and make evidence-based decisions about models, routing, prompts, and system changes. Build and lead a high-performing team of applied AI scientists and engineers; coach and develop team members. Partner closely with product, infrastructure, security, and application teams to align evaluation standards and deliver the highest-impact work. About you: 10+ years of experience in software engineering, ML infrastructure, data systems, or a related technical field. Experience must include building and operating production systems. 5+ years of engineering or applied AI team management experience, with a track record of technical leadership, developing engineers and scientists, and delivering cross-functional projects. Hands-on experience designing, building, or operating evaluation systems for LLM/GenAI products, including model-based evaluators or autograders; practical understanding of how to assess model, retrieval/RAG, assistant, or agent behavior. Familiarity with evaluation methods and tradeoffs: curated and production-derived datasets, benchmark creation, deterministic metrics, rubric-based and pairwise judgments, human review, judge validation and calibration, human-model alignment, and statistical analysis of results. Understanding of agent evaluation, including tool calling, multi-turn behavior, trajectory quality, task completion, and recovery from errors; experience with safety testing or red teaming is a plus. Strong coding ability in Python or another production language, with sound engineering fundamentals in testing, APIs, data modeling, and reliable distributed systems. Experience building scalable data and developer platforms, experiment pipelines, or CI/CD integrations; familiarity with cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, data stores, and observability is beneficial. Strong judgment about measurement quality, including dataset representativeness, judge calibration, reproducibility, uncertainty, and the risk of optimizing to a narrow metric. Knowledge of public benchmarks across domains and capabilities is a plus. Product-minded and collaborative: able to translate ambiguous quality goals into clear measures, communicate findings to technical and non-technical audiences, and influence roadmaps across teams. MS/PhD in Computer Science, AI or a related field. Location: This role is hybrid (4 days a week in our Mountain View office) Compensation & Benefits:

Available Location: Singapore About the Team The Cloudflare Customer Support Team solves complicated problems and answers technical questions via phone, email, chat and social media. Whether it is a Wordpress blogger using our services for free or a global Enterprise business with petabytes of web traffic, we are always eager to assist. We are the eyes and ears of Cloudflare, acting as the real-time voice of the customer to help communicate their needs and real-world use cases back to the rest of the company - for better service and future product development. What You'll Do Do you love solving complex technical issues and interacting with people? Are you passionate about providing premium-level support to customers and are a standout colleague? Cloudflare is seeking an experienced Technical Support Engineer for Application Services/Performance to join our team. You will work with our largest and most technically sophisticated customers on a variety of technical support issues to ensure they can deploy and operate Cloudflare's App Services solutions with confidence. Serve as a trusted technical advisor for our Enterprise customers, responding to and resolving inquiries and incidents related to Application Services/Performance, while delivering timely, high-quality and personalized assistance. Work directly with customers to diagnose, troubleshoot and resolve complex technical issues involving DNS, HTTP Errors, IAM, Load Balancing, Caching, CORS, SSL/TLS, Network, and other Application Services/Performance related configurations. Work with Engineering and Operations teams to remediate issues, suggest steps to mitigate, and apply the appropriate mitigation, when applicable. Create and maintain knowledge base articles, technical guides, and troubleshooting documentation for internal and customer use. You have a solid grasp of problem-solving with command line tools (dig/traceroute/curl/tcpdump). You have experience writing scripts in Bash, Python, JavaScript, or other scripting language. You have experience installing and configuring web servers like Apache, Nginx, and IIS. Work with Engineering and Product teams to improve products and tools. What We're Looking For You must have a minimum of 4 years’ experience working as a Technical Support Engineer supporting globally distributed reverse-proxy CDN platforms, with hands-on expertise in content caching, performance optimization, traffic routing, and edge delivery services similar to Cloudflare’s core network offerings. Exceptional troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with the ability to simplify complex concepts for customers. Strong customer service orientation and communication skills, both written and verbal. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. Strong understanding of L4/L7 protocols and concepts including, TCP/UDP, DNS, HTTP/S, IAM, Load Balancing, Caching, CORS, SSL/TLS, Network with a particular focus on Anycast concepts. Have experience using online diagnostic and monitoring platforms — including DNS lookup tools, global ping and traceroute testers, SSL/TLS configuration analyzers, and synthetic transaction or real-user monitoring services — to troubleshoot DNS resolution, network latency, certificate issues, and global service availability problems. Have experience using investigative observability tools such as Kibana, Grafana, Zabbix, Sentry, and live log-tailing utilities to analyze logs, trace issues, and pinpoint root causes of performance or reliability problems. Confident with command line and tools, including curl, dig, traceroute, openssl, git. Experience in a web development and / or hosting environment such as installing and configuring web servers like Apache, Nginx, Caddy and IIS. You are competent at writing scripts in Bash, Python, JavaScript or other scripting language. You have worked with PostgreSQL, MySQL, MS SQL, and other database servers. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field (or equivalent experience). Bonus Points For Experience in a shift-based or global support environment. Familiarity with SLA/KPI metrics and real-time queue management. What Makes Cloudflare Special? We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? jobs.title: Sr Digital Product Manager - R&D Commercialization & PPM
jobs.description: Career Category Information Systems Job Description The Senior Manager Product Manager will serve as a Digital Product Owner for a defined portfolio of R&D Commercialization technology products and systems and as the Amgen India (AIN) technology lead for R&D Commercialization and PPM. This role is accountable for translating R&D Commercialization business priorities into product roadmaps, investment priorities, delivery plans, and measurable technology outcomes. The individual will maintain primary relationships with key business stakeholders for their assigned product portfolio and ensure technology investments and team capacity remain aligned to the highest-value business needs. As the AIN lead for Commercialization, this individual will provide direct people leadership for AIN-based technology staff supporting Commercialization, including talent development, performance management, workforce planning, and building the skills and capabilities required to support an evolving Digital Product Operating Model (DPOM). The successful candidate will combine product ownership, business relationship management, people leadership, and technology delivery experience. The role will work closely with Digital Product Management leadership, Product Owners, Release Train/Delivery leadership, Business Analysts, Technical Leads, engineering teams, enterprise technology partners, and R&D Commercialization and PPM stakeholders. Key Roles and Responsibilities Digital Product Ownership & Product Strategy Serve as Product Owner for a defined portfolio of R&D Commercialization digital products, applications, data solutions, and technology capabilities. Develop and maintain product roadmaps aligned to R&D Commercialization priorities, business outcomes, enterprise technology strategy, and DPOM principles. Translate business needs and strategic priorities into clearly defined product capabilities, value drops, features, and prioritized backlogs. Own ongoing prioritization of demand within the assigned product portfolio, balancing business value, operational needs, technical sustainability, risk, dependencies, and available capacity. Partner with business stakeholders, Business Analysts, Technical Leads, and delivery teams to define product outcomes, requirements, acceptance criteria, and measures of success. Ensure product teams understand the business processes, users, outcomes, and value their products enable. Make day-to-day product prioritization and capacity decisions within established strategic and investment guardrails. Maintain visibility into product health, roadmap execution, value realization, risks, technical debt, and lifecycle needs. Business Stakeholder Relationship Management Serve as a primary technology relationship leader for designated R&D Commercialization business stakeholders and capability areas. Develop a deep understanding of Commercialization business processes, strategic priorities, operational challenges, and emerging technology, data, and AI opportunities. Build trusted relationships with business leaders and process owners and act as a strategic technology advisor rather than solely a delivery point of contact. Facilitate prioritization discussions that balance stakeholder demand with product strategy, technology capacity, enterprise standards, and expected business value. Partner with stakeholders to develop business cases, investment recommendations, roadmap priorities, and measurable product outcomes. Communicate product strategy, roadmap progress, delivery status, risks, dependencies, investment needs, and key decisions to business and technology leadership. Proactively identify opportunities where technology, data, automation, analytics, or AI can improve Commercialization outcomes. AIN Leadership & People Management Serve as the AIN technology lead for R&D Commercialization and PPM, providing leadership and coordination across AIN resources supporting the Commercialization and PPM technology portfolio. Directly manage assigned AIN Information Systems staff, including goal setting, performance management, coaching, career development, engagement, and talent planning. Recruit, interview, onboard, develop, and retain talent needed to support Commercialization's evolving digital product portfolio. Establish clear role expectations and ensure staff understand how their contributions connect to product outcomes and broader R&D priorities. Develop technical, product, business analysis, Agile, data, and AI capabilities within the AIN organization based on current and future portfolio needs. Coach staff toward greater ownership, independent decision-making, business understanding, and product-oriented ways of working. Support workforce and capacity planning across Commercialization product teams, including alignment of skills and resources to product demand. Foster strong collaboration between AIN and US-based staff and create an integrated global team operating model rather than location-based delivery silos. DPOM & Product Operating Model Leadership Champion adoption of Amgen's Digital Product Operating Model (DPOM) within the assigned Commercialization product portfolio. Help ensure delivery toward persistent product teams accountable for business outcomes and product lifecycle management. Establish clear product ownership, prioritization, decision rights, roadmap management, and stakeholder engagement practices. Partner with Release Train/Delivery leadership to establish effective execution practices across multiple product teams. Ensure business priorities and product roadmaps provide the direction for Agile planning and execution. Promote outcome-oriented product management, including clear measures of value and product performance. Partner with enterprise DPOM and Agile enablement organizations to align Commercialization ways of working with evolving enterprise standards. Portfolio, Investment & Governance Support annual and ongoing technology planning, budgeting, forecasting, and investment management for the assigned product portfolio. Develop and maintain appropriate business cases and investment recommendations for new capabilities, enhancements, lifecycle needs, and technology modernization. Partner with Digital Product Management leadership on investment governance and funding processes. Ensure products navigate applicable architecture, security, data, AI, technology, and investment governance processes and operate in compliance with standards. Balance investment across new business capabilities, operational sustainability, lifecycle requirements, technical debt, and innovation. Ensure appropriate product ownership exists across the full lifecycle—from discovery and investment through delivery, operation, enhancement, and retirement. Product Delivery & Operational Accountability Partner with Release Train Engineers, Scrum Masters, Technical Leads, Business Analysts, engineers, and other delivery roles to translate roadmaps into executable delivery plans. Participate actively in PI Planning, roadmap planning, backlog refinement, product reviews, and other key product and Agile ceremonies. Ensure product backlogs are appropriately prioritized and sufficiently mature to support effective team execution. Resolve product-level decisions and prioritization conflicts that could impede delivery. Monitor roadmap execution and adjust priorities based on business needs, capacity, risk, dependencies, and learning. Ensure appropriate ownership of production health, incidents, lifecycle needs, and operational sustainability for assigned products. Use operational, delivery, adoption, and value metrics to inform product decisions and continuous improvement. Technology, Data & AI Leadership Maintain sufficient understanding of the Commercialization technology landscape to make informed product and investment decisions. Partner closely with Technical Leads and enterprise architecture teams to ensure product roadmaps account for enterprise technology strategy, architecture standards, security, interoperability, and technical sustainability. Promote effective data management and FAIR data principles within product roadmaps and solution design. Identify and evaluate opportunities to apply automation, advanced analytics, AI, and emerging technologies to Commercialization business challenges. Ensure technology decisions balance near-term business value with long-term scalability, maintainability, and enterprise alignment. Required Functional Skills and Qualifications Must-Have Skills Significant experience in Information Systems, digital technology, product management, technology delivery, or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience owning or leading enterprise technology products, applications, platforms, or a portfolio of digital capabilities. Experience translating business strategy and stakeholder needs into product roadmaps, priorities, and technology outcomes. Demonstrated people-management experience, including coaching, performance management, talent development, and workforce planning. Strong business stakeholder relationship and influencing skills, including experience working with senior business and technology leaders. Experience working with Agile technology delivery teams and strong understanding of Product Owner responsibilities, backlog management, prioritization, and iterative delivery. Ability to balance competing business priorities, operational needs, technical considerations, risk, and finite technology capacity. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences. Experience leading or collaborating with globally distributed teams. Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity and organizational change. Preferred Experience Experience within R&D, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, life sciences, or another highly regulated environment. Experience with Digital Product Operating Models (DPOM) or transformation from project-oriented to product-oriented technology delivery. Experience operating as a Product Owner, Product Manager, Business Relationship Manager, or similar client-facing technology leader. Experience with SAFe Agile, Agile Release Trains, PI Planning, and scaled product delivery. Experience managing technology portfolios spanning applications (Salesforce), data (Databricks), analytics, automation, and AI capabilities. Experience with technology investment planning, budgeting, business cases, and portfolio governance. Experience managing globally distributed teams, particularly teams operating across United States and India locations. Product Owner, SAFe, Agile, or related product management certification is beneficial. .
